gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both entries identify the same theorem defect: liminf or best-iterate convergence does not justify the claimed monotone convergence of the raw objective values at the actual iterates. Both also identify the valid replacement using the running minimum.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The theorem incorrectly transfers a liminf/best-iterate guarantee into monotone convergence of the raw sequence, even though the method is not generally a descent method; monotonicity applies only to the running best values.

component_coverage.gold_component: The raw objective sequence is incorrectly claimed to decrease monotonically and converge from a result establishing only its liminf.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly contrasts liminf and best-iterate convergence with the unsupported monotone convergence claim for the actual iterates and notes that projected subgradient methods are not descent methods.

component_coverage.gold_component: The correct monotone conclusion concerns the running minimum, not the raw objective sequence.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction identifies the running minimum and supplies the specific repair of replacing the raw-sequence conclusion by monotone convergence of the best-iterate values.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold issue concerns the orientation and optimality of a triangular Cholesky right factor in the matrix objective, specifically replacing R^{-T} by R^{-1}. ISSUE-003 instead concerns an unsupported proof of Jacobi diagonal-scaling optimality and a gradient characterization, with an AM-GM/stationarity repair. It does not diagnose the triangular-factor orientation error or its counterexample.
